questions.question:
Which of the following statement(s) is/are CORRECT?

I. Oils containing unsaturated fatty acids should be used for cooking.

II Animal fats have saturated carbon chains.

III. Saturated fatty acids are generally harmful for health
questions.solution: Saturated fats are simply fat molecules that have no double bonds between carbon molecules because they are saturated with hydrogen molecules. Saturated fats are typically solid at room temperature. Some food items that contain saturated fats are fatty beef, pork, lamb etc.

questions.question: Which type of epithelial tissue forms the lining of kidney tubules and ducts of salivary glands, where it provides mechanical support?
questions.solution: Epithelial tissue forms a lining all over the body of the organism in order to protect the inner lying parts. They act as a barrier that keep the different body systems separate. Cuboidal epithelial tissue forms the lining of kidney tubules and ducts of salivary glands, where it provides mechanical support.

questions.question: Swollen bluish veins resulting from the valves that do not close properly are called ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**varicose veins.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Varicose veins are abnormally dilated, tortuous superficial veins caused by incompetent venous valves.
 
• They almost always affect the legs and feet.
 
• Veins have cup-like valves alternately open to allow blood flow towards the heart then close to prevent backflow.
 
• In varicose veins, the valves do not work properly allowing blood to pool in the vein, increasing venous pressure and like the hood of congestion, vein bulge, and twist.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Prevention from varicose veins:

 
 
• Lose weight
 
• Daily exercise
 
• Avoid standing for extended periods of time
 
• Should avoid injury
 
• Use compression socks

questions.question:
Which among the following constituents of the Xylem is/are tubular structure(s)?

I. Tracheids

II. Vessels

III. Xylem fibres
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only I and II.**__

__**Explanation:**__

 
• **Xylem** is a kind of tissue in vascular plants which transports nutrients and water from the roots to the leaves.
 
• It is composed of 4 types of cells, which are **tracheids**, **vessels**, **xylem fibres**, and **xylem parenchyma**. Of these, **xylem vessels** and **tracheids** are **tubular structures**.

questions.question: Which among the following forms a common passage for both the sperms and urine in human males?
questions.solution:
Testicles in human produce sperms and urine are formed in the kidney through filtration of blood.

 
• The sperm arrives first at the ampulla, where secretions from the seminal vesicle are added.
 
• From the ampulla, seminal fluid is propelled forward through the ejaculatory ducts toward the urethra.

The urinary tract is a pathway that includes the:

 
• Kidneys: two bean-shaped organs that filter waste from the blood and produce urine
 
• Ureters: two thin tubes that take pee from the kidney to the bladder
 
• Bladder: a sac that holds pee until it's time to go to the bathroom
 
• Urethra: the tube that carries urine from the bladder out of the body when you pee

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a valve of the Heart?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 3, i.e. **__Septum.__**

 
• The heart has four valves - one for each chamber of the heart.
 
• The valves keep blood moving through the heart in the right direction.
 
• The **mitral valve and tricuspid valve** are located between the atria (upper heart chambers) and the ventricles (lower heart chambers).
 
• The **aortic valve and pulmonic valve** are located between the ventricles and the major blood vessels leaving the heart.
 
• **The septum of the heart is the dividing wall between the right and left sides of the heart.**

questions.question: The sperms formed in the testes are delivered through the ______, which unites with a tube coming from the urinary bladder.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**vas deferens.**__

**__Explanation;__**

 
• The ‘vas deference is a long, muscular tube that travels from the epididymis into the pelvic cavity, to just behind the bladder. Hence, 3 is the correct answer.

 
• The vas deferens transports mature sperm to the urethra, the tube that carries urine or sperm outside of the body, in preparation for ejaculation.
 
• The sperm duct is also known as the vas deferens. They transport sperm into the penis. They also collect fluids secreted by different glands. These secretions are rich in proteins to enrich the sperm.

questions.question: By which process the cells of the meristematic tissue take up a permanent shape, size, and a function?
questions.solution:
The Corre answer is __Differentiation.__

__**Explanation:**__

Differentiation

 
• A permanent tissue is made up of mature, living, or dead cells divided from meristematic tissues. 
 
• In plants, meristematic tissue loses its ability to divide. After they take up a specific role.
 
• This process of taking up a permanent shape, size, and function of a meristematic tissue into a permanent tissue is called differentiation.
 
• The differentiation process causes the development of various types of permanent tissues
 
• Differentiation is the process in which cells of the root and the shoot apical meristems and the cambium mature to perform specific functions. In this process, lots of structural changes occur within the plant cell.
 
• For instance, The protoplasm is lost during the formation of tracheary elements.
 
• There are two types of Differentiation processes:
 
 
• Dedifferentiation process:
 
 
• In this process, the cells that have lost the capability to divide regain their dividing property under certain conditions.
 
• For instance, the formation of meristems from fully differentiated parenchymal cells. Dedifferentiation of normal cells in the human body leads to the formation of tumour cells.
 
 
 
• Redifferentiation process:
 
 
• Process in which differentiated cells that have lost their ability to divide are reformed from dedifferentiated cells and have the ability to perform specific functions.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Demarcation **is the action of fixing the limits of something. 
 
• ** Simplification:** is the process by which things are made less complicated so that they can be either done or understood

questions.question: Pineapple is a ______ plant.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Xerophyte.**__

__
 
• **Xerophytes** are plants that are able to survive in very** dry places.**
 
• They are generally found in areas like **deserts. **
 
• When water is abundant, their rate of transpiration is the same as other plants.
 
• In a prolonged drought, they have several survival mechanisms that make them successful.
 
• Popular examples of xerophytes are **cacti, pineapple.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Mesophytes** are terrestrial plants that need a moderate amount of water. For example **GoldenRod, Clover, etc.**
 
• **Hydrophytes **are the plants that live completely or partially submerged in freshwater.
 
 
• They have developed mechanisms for the removal of extra water from their cells.
 
• **Hydrophytes** have **broad leaves** with a large number of stomata on their upper surfaces.

questions.question: Which are the special proteins in muscles that contract and relax to cause movement?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** Contractile protein**

**Contractile protein:**

 
• Contractile protein is the special proteins in muscles that contract and relax to cause movement.
 
• The cytoplasm of cells is a colloidal network of contractile proteins.
 
• Actin filaments are the major components of this network.
 
• Other contractile proteins interact with this filament to create structural rigidity and movement.

questions.question: Which type of pathogen causes the water-borne disease Ascariasis?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Parasitic.**__

__**Explanation:**__

 
• Key facts about pathogens and the diseases caused by them:
 
• Parasitic type of pathogen causes the water-borne disease Ascariasis.
 
• It is a roundworm organism found in the small intestine and mostly occurs in children.
 
• The infection takes place by eating food or drinking contaminated water with Ascaris eggs from human excreta.
 
• Abdominal pain, Abdominal swelling, shortness of breathing, fever and diarrhoea are the main symptoms of this disease.
 
• Ascaris is a commonly found parasitic worm in humans.
 
• Ascariasis, a type of helminthiasis, is one of the groups of neglected tropical diseases. 
 
• This disease is prevalent worldwide, especially in tropical and subtropical countries.

questions.question:
Which of the following groups is/are called phanerogams?

I. Thallophyte

II. Bryophyte

III. Pteridophyte
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**No option is correct**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The plant kingdom is divided into 2-sub kingdoms, Cryptogams and Phanerogams.
 
 
• Cryptogams are flowerless and seedless plants that produce spores. They include thallophytes, bryophytes, and pteridophytes. Examples: fern, liverworts, etc
 
• Phanerogams are seed-bearing plants that include angiosperms and gymnosperms. Examples: pine, petunia, etc.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Thallophyte**

 
 
• They are commonly called algae.
 
• The plant body is not differentiated from roots, stems, and leaves.
 
• Examples: spirogyra, Ulothrix, etc.
 
 
 
• Bryophytes:
 
 
• They are often referred to as amphibians of the plant kingdom.
 
• These are small terrestrial plants.
 
• They show differentiation in the body design, with stem, leaf-like structures, and root-like structures.
 
• Examples: Funaria, Marchantia, etc.
 
 
 
• Pteridophyta:
 
 
• These plants are having specialized tissue for conduction.
 
• The plant body is differentiated into roots, stems, and leaves.
 
• Examples: Fern, Marsilea, etc.

questions.question: Build-up of which acid in our muscles during sudden activity causes cramps?
questions.solution:
• Whenever sudden activity of a muscle takes place the muscles cannot be supplied with enough oxygen.
 
• To satisfy the need of energy anaerobic respiration takes place forming lactic acid as the by product. Lactic acid causes pain and stiffness in the muscles.

questions.question: In 2020, the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine was awarded jointly to Harvey J Alter, Michael Houghton and Charles M Rice for the discovery of:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**hepatitis C virus**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **In 2020, the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine was awarded jointly to Harvey J Alter, Michael Houghton, and Charles M Rice for the discovery of the hepatitis C virus**__.

 __
 
• The methodical studies of transfusion-associated hepatitis by 2020 Medicine Laureate Harvey J. Alter demonstrated that an unknown virus was a common cause of chronic hepatitis.
 
• Michael Houghton – awarded the 2020 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine – used an untested strategy to isolate the genome of the new virus that was named Hepatitis C virus.
 
• Medicine Laureate Charles M. Rice provided the final evidence showing that the Hepatitis C virus alone could cause hepatitis
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hepatitis, from the Greek name for liver and inflammation, is a disease characterized by poor appetite, vomiting, fatigue and jaundice – yellow discoloration of the skin and eyes**.

 
 
• Chronic hepatitis leads to liver damage, which may progress to cirrhosis and liver cancer.
 
• Viral infection is the leading cause of hepatitis, with some forms persisting without symptoms for many years before life-threatening complications develop.

questions.question: In sexual reproduction the male gametes are generally ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Both motile and small__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

**In sexual reproduction, the male gametes (sperm cells) are generally both motile and small.**

 
• **Motility:** Male gametes are typically motile, meaning they have the ability to move on their own. This is primarily achieved through the flagellum, a whip-like structure that propels the sperm forward. The motility of sperm is crucial for successful fertilization, as sperm need to travel through the female reproductive tract to reach and penetrate the egg.
 
• **Size: **Male gametes are also generally smaller compared to female gametes (eggs). This small size allows sperm to be produced in large quantities and is advantageous for their role in fertilization. Smaller size facilitates easier movement and efficiency in reaching the egg, increasing the chances of successful fertilization.
 
• The human males have **23 pairs of chromosomes** including XY sex chromosomes. Therefore the male gametes has 22 chromosomes and either an X or a Y chromosome. Thus male gametes can be of two types:22+X or 22+Y.
 
• Female gametes are called** egg or ova.**

questions.question: Many marine animals use ________ dissolved in sea-water to make their shells.

**__Explanation:__**

 
• Marine animals use calcium carbonates for making their shells while using the process of Ocean Acidification. Calcium carbonates are found in abundance in seawater.
 
• Animals make hard shells from calcium carbonates. This process is called coastal acidification.

questions.question: Plants of which group are predominantly aquatic?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Thallophyta.**__

__**Explanation:**__

Thallophyta:

 
• Thallophytes are organisms that possess a thallus-like body.
 
• The body is not differentiated into stems, roots and leaves.
 
• They are tracheophytes (vascular tissues are absent).
 
• Lichens and algae fall under thallophyta.

 Bryophyta:

 
• They are tracheophytes, archegoniate, and amphibious cryptogams.
 
• Various mosses and liverworts fall under the classification of Bryophyta.
 
• They are commonly found growing in moist and shaded areas in the hills.
 
• Bryophytes can live in the soil, but they depend on water for sexual reproduction.
 
• They have a thallus-like body and possess rootlike and leaf-like structures.
 
• Their main plant body is haploid.

 Pteridophyta:

 
• They are archegoniate, embryophytes, tracheophytes cryptogams.
 
• Ferns and horsetails fall under the Pteridophyta.
 
• They are found growing in cool, damp, shady places. They also grow well in sandy soils.
 
• Evolutionarily they are the first plants to possess the vascular system- xylem and phloem.

questions.question: Which meristem increases the length of the stems and the roots?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Apical Meristem__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Apical Meristem** increases the length of the roots and stem as it produces auxin which is a plant hormone.
 
• It can be found at the tips of the shoot and root of a plant.
 
• The actual apical meristem is a** cluster of densely packed and undifferentiated cells. **
 
• In the shoot apical meristem, cells are only created in **one direction. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lateral meristem**

 
 
• Plants use** lateral meristem tissue to grow in diameter **as part of secondary growth.
 
• There are two types of lateral meristematic tissue—**the vascular cambium and the cork cambium.**
 
 
 
• **Intercalary meristem**
 
 
• The intercalary tissue in the middle of the plant is **capable of rapid growth and regrowth**.
 
• The intercalary tissue at the base of a** blade of grass allows it to regrow **after being cut.
